records.title: VanderPlas, Understanding the Lomb–Scargle Periodogram
records.locator: arXiv HTML lines 65–71; Section III on observing windows; Section VI lines 424–455 on white-noise assumptions and correlated-error formulation; Section VII.4.2 lines 611–662 on search-wide false-alarm probability, bootstrap caveats, and interpretation.
records.access_utc: 2026-10-10T07:06:21Z–2026-10-10T07:10:40Z; exact individual page timestamps were not exposed
records.retrieval_operation: Opened the primary arXiv record and inspected the paper discussion of periodogram assumptions and practical interpretation.
records.observed_operation: Explains Lomb–Scargle for unevenly sampled observations and discusses observing-window structure, aliases, frequency-grid choices, maximum-peak false-alarm assessment, and correlated-error modeling. The simple statistical guarantees assume uncorrelated white noise; its described ordinary bootstrap holds times fixed and resamples observed values.
records.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Window structure can create aliases. Single-frequency or white-noise significance does not account by itself for the maximum over a frequency search. The paper states that the ordinary value-resampling bootstrap does not correctly account for correlated noise and that false-alarm probability does not answer the probability the dataset is periodic. A null method must fit actual dependence and sampling; no universal method is selected for this unknown case.
records.applicability: Guides a future preregistered periodicity analysis after timestamps, candidate-selection rules, sampling window, and dependence are known. No periodogram or significance was computed.
records.research_phase: post-release draft supplementation; frozen discovery unchanged

critic.join: ZTF page describes a public telescope survey and its own releases; TESS page describes spacecraft images, target pixels, and downstream products. The case brief separately identifies the teaching archive as nightly images and says no data were supplied. Neither source establishes this target's actual coverage or whether a proposed third-party product shares inputs.
AAVSO atmospheric section states same-degree attenuation for target and comparisons as the cancellation condition; cloud spatial uniformity alone is not equated with same-degree measured effect.
IRAF task parameter table and output section define the task-level defaults and the blank-output replacement condition; no case reducer is identified.
AIJ guide's Astrometry Settings name the raw re-save toggle and its consequence; separate Data Processor section does not make that warning universal.

Astropy example joins a Time object carrying observer location, a source SkyCoord passed to light_travel_time, and TDB addition; documentation does not address arbitrary time labels imported from elsewhere.

reviser.join: ZTF and TESS source documentation establishes separate survey/spacecraft products and their processing stages. It does not establish target coverage or case-level data lineage; reprocessed teaching exposures remain non-independent.
The AAVSO example specifies same-degree effects on target and comparison stars, and says the cancellation case is rare; spatial uniformity alone is not asserted to suffice.
IRAF 2.18 ccdproc's parameter table and output section support the named-task defaults, preconditions, subset selection, and blank-output replacement; they do not identify the case reducer.

The AIJ guide separates Data Processor work from the named Astrometry Settings Re-save Raw Science option; only that enabled operation is tied to the WCS-added original science FITS overwrite warning.

reviser.scope: SCW-05 barycentric calculation versus time label
reviser.join: Astropy's example and AIJ's calculated-header-metadata workflow use target and observer coordinates for computation; neither makes reading a pre-existing BJD_TDB label itself a computation.
The expanded official page context, lines 103–109, directly states the public DR24 observation cutoff through 22 October 2025; the critic's cited lines 73–102 stopped before that subsection.
The primary paper supports dependence-aware and search-wide future analysis, while leaving the suitable null procedure unresolved until real cadence and residual dependence are known.
The current Photutils guide supports a declared background-subtracted input and controlled overlap-method comparison, not a claim about the archive reducer.
